scalesUsed.notes: A - B - C# - D - E - F# - G# - A
scalesUsed.application: Drives the uplifting melodic lead hooks and anthemic vocal choruses
Underpins the sparkling octave fills and synth-guitar counter-melodies

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Euphoric A major Ionian energy driven by 160 BPM post-punk rhythm and shimmering chorus textures
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: F# minor is the relative minor of A major

mainProgression.description: The immortal 50s doo-wop progression turbocharged with 160 BPM Australian pub-rock drive, syncopated downstrokes, and lush Roland JC-120 chorus modulation.

sectionProgressions.description: Explosive four-chord stadium hook featuring full-band unison energy and soaring lead melodies
Taut two-chord pendulum maintaining steady pulse beneath Michael Hutchence's rhythmic vocal delivery
Pivots to the supertonic Bm before climbing through D and dominant E to relaunch the chorus

harmonicFunction: A (I) - Grounded tonic foundation establishing the bright, life-affirming tonal center
F#m (vi) - Relative minor providing momentary emotional shadow without losing forward speed
D (IV) - Warm subdominant chord opening up the melodic horizon
E (V) - Dominant resolution driving inexorably back to the A major home chord
Bm (ii) - Darker minor pivot introducing contrast into the bridge

techniques.name: High-Tempo Post-Punk Downstrokes
techniques.description: Consistent, driving eighth-note downstroke rhythm at 160 BPM with fret-hand muting between changes

sequence: Lock into the 160 BPM pulse with tight wrist rotation
Accent beats 2 and 4 to lock with the snare backbeat
Keep barre-chord fretting relaxed to avoid forearm fatigue over 4 minutes
tips: Use a 0.73mm to 0.88mm plectrum for flexible snap without pick drag
Alternate between open voicings and 5th-position barre chords to match the studio track's layered texture
Engage an analog chorus pedal (Boss CE-2) for the authentic 1982 new-wave sparkle

sections.name: Intro Riff & Progression
sections.description: Iconic synth and guitar fanfare launching straight into the driving I - vi - IV - V progression.
notes: Clean transitions between A and F#m
Let the open high E and B strings ring on the final E chord

sections.name: Verse Rhythm
sections.description: Two-chord A to D groove with subtle palm muting and chorus shimmer.
notes: Mute slightly near the bridge saddles for a tighter punch
Accentuate the upbeat push into each chord change

sections.name: Chorus Fanfare
sections.description: Full-volume chorus burst on 'Don't change for the crime of being you'.
notes: Unleash full dynamic range with ringing open strings
Hit the F#m barre with solid pressure on the lower strings

guitar.pickup: Bridge or bridge/middle position for crisp treble cut

amp.recommended: Roland JC-120 Jazz Chorus or Fender Twin Reverb

effects.distortion: Light transparent overdrive (Ibanez TS9 / Boss BD-2)
effects.other: Analog Chorus (Boss CE-2) and digital delay set to dotted eighth notes

beginner.title: Open Chords & Steady Quarter Notes
steps: Practice transitions between open A, F#m (or F#m7), D, and E chords
Play steady quarter-note downstrokes at 100 BPM with metronome
Memorize the verse A - D two-chord pattern
beginner.goals: Clean chord changes without hesitations at half tempo

intermediate.title: Speed Ladder to 160 BPM
steps: Ramp tempo from 120 to 160 BPM using our Metronome Speed Trainer
Incorporate eighth-note downstrokes with accents on beats 2 and 4
Engage chorus pedal and practice barre chord transitions at fret 2 and 5
intermediate.goals: Full song playthrough at 160 BPM without forearm tension

advanced.title: Lead Fills & Studio Layering
steps: Learn Tim Farriss's soaring octave melodic fills across strings 1 and 3
Master syncopated 16th-note rhythm chops during the second verse
Dial in authentic analog chorus and dotted-eighth delay trails
advanced.goals: Stage-ready live performance with authentic Australian pub-rock punch

commonMistakes: Tensing the picking forearm at 160 BPM leading to cramping by verse 2
Rushing the transition between D and E at the end of the chorus
Fretting the F#m barre chord with insufficient pressure on the 3rd and 2nd strings
practiceRoutine: Warm up with chromatic alternate picking drills at 120 BPM
Run the A - F#m - D - E progression for 5 minutes straight at 140 BPM
Play along with the original recording focusing on rhythm pocket
focusAreas: Relaxed right-wrist motion at high tempos
Clean barre-chord hand shifts between frets 2, 5, and open
Dynamic contrast between intimate verse and explosive chorus
metronomeWork: Start at 110 BPM with quarter-note clicks
Increase by +5 BPM every 4 bars using our Speed Trainer
Hold steady at the target 160 BPM for three consecutive runs
